title: Build, persistence and application submission
goal: Complete a checkable Nexus project with GUI, data, tests, portable sources, an exact submission revision and a defense.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–5: functions, STL, ownership, testing and multi-file builds.
Study the linked prerequisite topics below before this lesson.

sections.title: A build is a reproducible process
paragraphs: Sources are not the same as a running application. Project files, CMake settings, target and SDK version determine the build result. The checked pilot uses Qt 6.8.3 and Emscripten 3.1.56; console C++20 uses another runtime. Record these details in README without promising compatibility with arbitrary Qt or browser versions that have not been tested.

A build belongs to a source snapshot. Editing after launch means the old Preview does not establish that the new text works. Check revision status, rebuild and repeat the scenario. Build diagnostics, model tests and interface checks provide different results. A build-service connection error is not a learner variable-declaration error.

sections.title: Saving application data into the project
paragraphs: TaskFlow serializes NXTF1 into the permitted taskflow.txt. First select Save application data inside the application, then use the Studio panel’s data-save action and confirm the file in the project. After Stop and a new run, the list should be restored. A file existing only in a running Preview does not establish persistence after closing it.

Before corruption tests, retain the valid file and a checkpoint. In a copy, change the version marker and verify explicit rejection rather than silent reinterpretation. Restore the valid file afterwards. Do not experiment on the only copy of a personal project or clear storage and cookies; those actions are unnecessary for checking the teaching format.

sections.title: Tests and independent extension
paragraphs: The TaskFlow starter already demonstrates adding, completing, rejection and roundtrip. Copying the finished example is not a complete independent project. The module project requires open/completed counts and an all/open view filter that preserves ids. An alternative route is an agreed equivalent feature with explained outcomes and tests.

Specify the filter contract before editing and prepare tasks with different statuses. Check that filtering does not delete model data, completing after filtering uses the correct id and saving includes every task. Run model tests separately from the GUI. Evaluation also requires tests for the extension and a defense involving a small new command.

sections.title: A toggle button and filter state
paragraphs: QPushButton supports a checkable mode: setCheckable(true) enables checking, isChecked() reads the checked state and toggled reports its change. This differs from enabled: interaction availability and checked state are separate properties. Connect toggled to refresh with this as context. Filtering changes displayed rows only, while open/done counts use the entire model. In Nexus Preview, focus the named Open tasks only control: a visible ring identifies the target, Space and Enter activate it, and another activation restores the full view. For an ordinary Qt button, Space with focus is the basic activation key; outside Nexus, Enter depends on default/autoDefault and the window type.

Check two tasks: complete the first, enable filtering and complete the remaining second task. Its id remains two even though it is now the first visible row. Open: 0 Done: 2 verifies that scenario; saved NXTF1 must still contain both tasks. Changing the filter requires no change to TaskModel or its data format.

sections.title: Exact submission and feedback
paragraphs: Immutable submission takes place in Final assessment, where the exam, selected project and control change are checked automatically. Later edits do not rewrite submitted sources. Inspect the snapshot version in history. Studio checkpoints and ZIP preserve this module’s training TaskFlow; use the separate assignment starter and its contract for the final submission. Green tests do not assess arbitrary extensions or prove authorship. Teacher review is a future optional route, not a requirement for course completion.

The project rubric considers correctness and boundaries, tests, resource ownership, architecture, complexity reasoning and reproducibility. Supply sources, synthetic sample data, actual observations and a short ADR. Personal code is not published automatically. Feedback should identify an observed issue and a next correction step rather than giving only a total score.

sections.title: Portability and assessment boundaries
paragraphs: The source ZIP contains model, GUI, CLI, tests, CMake and instructions. Building the model and CLI externally needs no Qt; the graphical build requires a compatible SDK. This is optional portability: required execution and submission happen in Nexus. Check archive paths and file bytes; downloading a ZIP alone does not establish that its project builds.

The module project concludes event-application teaching but does not replace a separate examination spanning all six modules. Unfamiliar-code work and an independent final project need their own approved assessment rules. Distinguish studied topics, a checked application, a graded submission and assessment still outstanding. This lesson does not automatically issue a certificate.

sections.title: Laboratory contract: input to observation
paragraphs: In a new TaskFlow project implement open/done counts and an all/open GUI filter. Filtering must preserve the model, persistent ids and all NXTF1 data. Verify persistence, Stop→Run, model tests, a Studio checkpoint and portable ZIP within Nexus. For immutable final submission open Final assessment and use its starter.

Trace the first reference scenario before running. Enter learn C++ and press Enter. One open task; the count reflects the model. Relate each algorithm step to state changes, distinguishing rejection from the point where a change is committed.

sections.title: Reading a working example
paragraphs: The total count comes from tasks().size(). Model code and NXTF1 remain unchanged. This is the starting reference before adding a filter. First identify data, ownership and the observable outcome. Then change exactly one initial condition and predict which observation changes. This connects syntax to a contract rather than memorizing finished source text.

The filter skips done items only while rendering. UserRole continues to store the persistent id. Saving records all tasks regardless of the filter. Compare the second example with the first: what new boundary is covered, and which test distinguishes the correct implementation from a superficially similar mistake? Retain both sources, predictions and actual observations so that the explanation can be reproduced.

sections.title: Independent checking and transfer
paragraphs: Prepare ZIP, README, ADR and a restoration check. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Begin with a specification and input bounds; the worked function is a scaffold, not the requirements of another domain. State an independent expectation before execution so that a test is not fitted to accidental output.

Defend the project by adding a small new scenario. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Record decisions, a rejected alternative, checked scenarios and remaining limitations. Independently complete the final assessment control-change task and explain which files, tests and observations it affects. An additional peer or teacher requirement is optional review.

selfcheck.prompt: One of two tasks is done and the open filter is enabled. What are total counts and model size?
options: Open 1/Done 1, model size 2, one visible row.
selfcheck.feedback: The filter excludes rows only from the view. Counts and persistence use the whole model, including the hidden completed task.

selfcheck.prompt: After immutable submission, the learner edits workspace src/gui.cpp. What should the teacher read in the earlier submission?
options: A mixture of old model and new GUI depending on opening time.
The snapshot bytes recorded by that submission.
The current workspace without hash verification.
selfcheck.feedback: An immutable submission belongs to a specific revision. Later edits require another submission rather than rewriting the earlier one.

selfcheck.prompt: Baseline tests pass, but a new filter was added. How should the extension be assessed?
options: Treat every new GUI feature as automatically fully tested.
Add filter scenarios, verify ids/data and apply the rubric with defense.
selfcheck.feedback: Baseline covers specified original cases. A new feature may break visibility or identity without affecting those checks.

selfcheck.prompt: What is required after downloading a portable source ZIP?
options: Treat the.zip extension as proof of portability.
Add session credentials to README for the model build.
Restore into a separate copy, build and test selected data/scenarios.
selfcheck.feedback: An archive enables transfer but is not its verification result. Model/CLI builds require no Nexus session, and credentials are excluded.

selfcheck.prompt: How can accessible Open tasks only be tested in Nexus Preview without calling click from test JavaScript?
options: Change only DOM checked and consider the model verified.
Check only the filter label in a screenshot.
Focus the named control, press Space/Enter and verify the C++ view/preserved ids.
selfcheck.feedback: The keyboard path must actually invoke the Qt/C++ action. A DOM flag and a picture alone prove neither the handler nor model preservation.

selfcheck.prompt: Explain data saving versus source submission.
selfcheck.feedback: The module concludes with a learning project. Separate course-wide assessment remains a later stage; topic completion does not replace grading and defense.

practice.title: Laboratory: Build, persistence and application submission
practice.task: In a new TaskFlow project implement open/done counts and an all/open GUI filter. Filtering must preserve the model, persistent ids and all NXTF1 data. Verify persistence, Stop→Run, model tests, a Studio checkpoint and portable ZIP within Nexus. For immutable final submission open Final assessment and use its starter.

files.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(TaskFlow LANGUAGES CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
add_library(task_model src/task_model.cpp)
target_include_directories(task_model PUBLIC include)
if(EMSCRIPTEN)
 target_compile_options(task_model PUBLIC -fexceptions)
 target_link_options(task_model INTERFACE -fexceptions)
endif()
add_executable(taskflow_cli src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(taskflow_cli PRIVATE task_model)
enable_testing()
add_executable(taskflow_tests tests/task_model_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(taskflow_tests PRIVATE task_model)
add_test(NAME task_model COMMAND taskflow_tests)
option(NEXUS_GUI "Build the Qt GUI" OFF)
if(EMSCRIPTEN)
 set(NEXUS_GUI ON)
endif()
if(NEXUS_GUI)
 find_package(Qt6 6.8 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Widgets)
 qt_add_executable(program MANUAL_FINALIZATION src/gui.cpp)
 target_link_libraries(program PRIVATE task_model Qt6::Widgets)
 if(EMSCRIPTEN)
  target_compile_options(program PRIVATE -fexceptions)
  target_link_options(program PRIVATE -fexceptions -sDISABLE_EXCEPTION_CATCHING=0 -sDYNAMIC_EXECUTION=0 "-sEXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS=['FS']" -sALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1)
 endif()
 qt_finalize_executable(program)
endif()

# TaskFlow — portable C++20 project

In Nexus use Project Studio to edit, build, run, test and submit.
Optional native model/CLI build: cmake -S . -B build -DNEXUS_GUI=OFF; cmake --build build; ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure.
GUI: Qt 6.8.3; WebAssembly: Emscripten 3.1.56.
Data: taskflow.txt / NXTF1. Preserve old projects and never include credentials.

cases.label: Ordinary addition
cases.input: Enter learn C++ and press Enter.
cases.output: One open task; the count reflects the model.

cases.label: Empty title
cases.input: Leave the input empty and activate Add task.
cases.output: A validation error; task count is unchanged.

cases.label: Whitespace title
cases.input: Enter three spaces and press Enter.
cases.output: Rejection; input remains available for correction.

cases.label: Complete without selection
cases.input: Activate Complete selected with an empty list.
cases.output: Select a task feedback; the model is unchanged.

cases.label: Repeated title
cases.output: Two tasks with distinct ids: duplicate titles are permitted.

cases.label: Explicit persistence
cases.input: Add a task; save application data, save through the panel, Stop and Run.
cases.output: The task is restored from taskflow.txt and sources are preserved.

cases.label: Selecting a persistent id
cases.input: Add two tasks, select the second and complete it.
cases.output: Only the second task is completed; repetition does not increase done.

cases.label: Stop and continue
cases.input: Stop Preview, change a C++ label and rebuild.
cases.output: New build text appears; an earlier submitted revision stays unchanged.

cases.label: Filtering preserves persistent ids
cases.input: Add alpha and beta, complete alpha, enable Open tasks only and complete the remaining beta.
cases.output: Open: 0 Done: 2; both tasks are retained and filtering does not delete the model.

cases.label: Saving with an active filter
cases.input: After the preceding scenario save data and stop/restart the application.
cases.output: NXTF1 contains both tasks; restarting with no filter shows both completed items.

cases.label: Submission revision
cases.input: Submit the checked version, then change only a label in the current project.
cases.output: Submission history retains the old snapshot; a new build belongs to the changed sources.

criteria: The full input and output contract is satisfied.
Invariants and lifetimes are explained; rejection preserves the model.
Ordinary, empty, boundary and failure scenarios are covered.
Add an all/open filter preserving ids.
An independent extension and test are supplied, rather than only a reference copy.
Sources, actual observations and limits of conclusions are retained.
practice.hint: Do not compute total done using only visible QListWidget rows.

A condition preserved at the boundaries of permitted model operations.

rubric.complete: Adding, completing, rejection, filtering and restoration are checked without losing model data.
rubric.partial: The primary scenario works but some boundaries remain unchecked.
rubric.missing: Data loss, incorrect ids or a broken required scenario remain.

rubric.complete: Model tests, a GUI protocol, an independent case and a detected mutation are supplied.
rubric.partial: Tests repeat the example with insufficient independent expectations.
rubric.missing: No reproducible test exists, or FAIL does not make verification fail.

rubric.complete: Model, QObject and callback ownership are explained; destruction and disconnection are checked.
rubric.partial: Ownership is partly explained and closure checks are incomplete.
rubric.missing: A dangling pointer, double deletion or unjustified ownership cycle remains.

rubric.complete: The model is independent of Qt, filtering belongs to the view and changes are localized.
rubric.partial: Responsibilities are mostly separated but one is duplicated or hidden.
rubric.missing: Rules depend on widgets and cannot be tested independently.

rubric.complete: Structures, the 200-task limit, refresh cost and queue/step bounds are explained.
rubric.partial: Complexity is named without relating it to input size or the actual algorithm.
rubric.missing: Bounds are unexplained or unsupported parallelism is claimed.

rubric.complete: README, SDK/target, source ZIP, exact submission, observations and an independent defense are supplied.
rubric.partial: Artifacts exist but rebuilding or explaining a new command is incomplete.
rubric.missing: The build is not reproducible or submission differs from the demonstrated source.
